verdict: Topstep costs $49 a month for 50K and has a published route to a live account, while Apex does not show its new evaluation prices outside checkout in every country. Apex sells a one-time evaluation with no consistency rule and a choice of drawdown, but closes each funded account after six payouts. Both cap 50K drawdown at $2,000 and both ban holding past the close.
body:
Which to pick

Pick Topstep if you want a low monthly entry price and an end-of-day drawdown on every account. Pick Apex if you want to pass fast in one payment and prefer no consistency target in the evaluation. Apex blocks some countries entirely, so check that it serves yours.

blurb: Two of the largest forex firms, rule by rule
verdict: Both sell a 50K two-step challenge with a static 10% max loss and a refundable fee. FTMO (€345) has the longer track record and a 4.8 Trustpilot score; FundedNext ($299.99, in US dollars) is likely cheaper depending on the exchange rate, also sells futures, but bans EAs on CFD accounts of $50K and above.
body:
Which to pick

Pick FTMO for the longer track record and if you use EAs on a 50K account. Pick FundedNext if you want futures and CFDs from one firm or a lower price. FundedNext's 2-Step asks for 8% then 5%; FTMO's asks for 10% then 5%.

verdict: Both charge one time for the evaluation. Tradeify has no activation fee, end-of-day drawdown on every plan and allows news trading; Apex lets you choose intraday or end-of-day drawdown and has no evaluation consistency rule, but caps each funded account at six payouts.
body:
Which to pick

Tradeify is easier to model: one price, no activation fee, end-of-day drawdown. Apex suits traders who want no consistency target while passing and can work with the six-payout limit.

blurb: Two of the cheapest one-time 50K evaluations
verdict: Lucid ($136 for LucidFlex) and Tradeify ($145 for Growth) are two of the cheapest one-time 50K evaluations we track, both with end-of-day drawdown and no activation fee. Lucid allows bots and has no consistency rule once funded on LucidFlex; Tradeify allows only your own non-HFT bots and adds a 35% rule to Growth payouts.
body:
Which to pick

Pick Lucid if you trade with your own automation or copiers. Pick Tradeify if you want a choice of payout styles (Select Flex or Select Daily). Lucid restricts more countries, so check that it serves yours.

verdict: Topstep is cheaper to start ($49 a month for 50K against $170 at Take Profit Trader) and keeps an end-of-day drawdown in its funded account. Take Profit Trader lets you withdraw from your first funded day once the balance is above its $52,000 buffer, but its PRO account switches to an intraday trailing drawdown and pays 80% until you reach PRO+.
body:
Which to pick

Pick Topstep if the monthly cost and an end-of-day drawdown matter most. On its Standard path you pay $49 a month plus a $149 activation fee once you pass, or $95 a month with no activation fee. Pick Take Profit Trader if you want access to withdrawals early and are comfortable with an intraday trailing drawdown once funded. Its PRO activation fee is $130.

Rules that trip people up

Topstep's Combine has a best-day limit of 55% of the profit target. Going over it raises the target instead of failing you. Take Profit Trader's Test requires your best day to stay under 50% of total profit. On news, Take Profit Trader's PRO accounts must be flat from one minute before to one minute after events such as FOMC, NFP and CPI. Topstep only bans purposely trading your full maximum size into a scheduled major news event.

verdict: Bulenox gives its 50K end-of-day account a wider $2,500 drawdown, has no consistency rule in the Qualification and allows news trading with no blackout window, for $175 one-time. Apex keeps the 50K drawdown at $2,000 and pays 100% of approved payouts on its performance accounts. It also adds a 50% consistency rule once you are funded and closes each performance account after six payouts. Apex's current evaluation prices were not shown on its site when we checked.
body:
Which to pick

Pick Bulenox if you want more room on a 50K account and trade around news releases. Pick Apex if you want to keep all of each approved payout and do not mind its funded consistency rule and six-payout limit per account. Neither firm lets you hold positions overnight. Apex does not allow automated trading at all. Bulenox needs management approval for third-party algorithms.

Getting to a live account

Both decide at their discretion. Bulenox may consider traders for a live account after three successful payouts. Apex says it may move a trader to live at any time, and lists three consecutive withdrawals from one account as one guideline.

verdict: Take Profit Trader charges $170 a month for a 50K Test and lets funded PRO traders withdraw from the first day above the buffer. Apex sells one-time evaluations with no consistency rule, and pays 100% of approved payouts on its performance accounts. It limits each performance account to six payouts. Neither firm allows bots.
body:
Which to pick

Pick Take Profit Trader if you want withdrawals available early. Its PRO account pays 80%, or 90% on PRO+, and needs the balance above $52,000 on 50K before the first withdrawal. Pick Apex if you would rather pay once and keep 100% of approved payouts, and you can live with a funded consistency rule: no single day may be 50% or more of profit since the last payout.

Drawdown

Both use a $2,000 maximum loss on 50K. Take Profit Trader trails at end of day in the Test and intraday in PRO. Apex lets you choose an end-of-day or an intraday trailing evaluation.

verdict: Tradeify charges once ($145 for a 50K Growth evaluation, with no activation fee). Topstep charges $49 a month plus a $149 activation fee on its Standard path. If you pass in the first month, Topstep's Standard path costs $198 in total against $145 at Tradeify. Both use a $2,000 end-of-day trailing drawdown on 50K and pay 90%.
body:
Which to pick

Pick Tradeify if you want a single payment, trade news (it has no news rule), or want an instant funded account (Lightning Funded). Pick Topstep if you prefer a low monthly entry. It also offers a $95-a-month path with no activation fee.

Consistency rules

Tradeify's Growth evaluation has no consistency rule, but every funded payout request must pass a 35% rule. Its Select evaluation limits any day to 40% of total profit. Topstep's Combine limits your best day to 55% of the profit target and raises the target if you go over. Its Standard funded account has no consistency rule.

verdict: The5ers High Stakes is cheaper ($249 for 50K against €345 for FTMO's 2-Step) and asks for the same targets of 10% and then 5%. Its loss limits are tighter: 8% maximum and 4% daily, against 10% and 5% at FTMO. FTMO allows EAs within platform limits, while The5ers needs written approval for automated trading.
body:
Which to pick

Pick FTMO if you want more room before a breach and plan to use EAs. Pick The5ers if price matters more and your risk per day stays well inside 4%. Both pay 80% at the start with a scaling plan that raises it. Both pay the first reward after 14 days.

News trading

Both restrict it on funded accounts in a similar way. FTMO bars order execution 2 minutes before and after selected high-impact news on its standard funded accounts. The5ers' High Stakes forbids new orders 2 minutes before and after high-impact news.

verdict: MyFundedFutures sells one-time evaluations (from $153 for a 50K Builder) with no activation fee. Topstep charges $49 a month plus a $149 activation fee on its Standard path. Both use a $2,000 end-of-day drawdown on 50K evaluations. MyFundedFutures pays more often (every 48 hours on Builder, daily on Rapid), but Builder pays 80% against Topstep's 90%.
body:
Which to pick

Pick MyFundedFutures if you want frequent payouts and a single payment. Its Rapid plan pays 90%, but its sim funded account uses an intraday trailing drawdown. Rapid EOD keeps it at end of day for a higher price. Pick Topstep if you prefer a monthly price and an end-of-day drawdown in the funded account.

News trading

MyFundedFutures requires you to be flat from 2 minutes before to 2 minutes after Tier 1 releases on Rapid and Pro funded accounts. It allows news trading in every evaluation and on Builder. Topstep only bans purposely trading your full maximum size into a scheduled major news event.

verdict: Lucid sells its 50K LucidFlex evaluation for a one-time $136 with no activation fee, and LucidFlex has no consistency rule once funded. Topstep costs $49 a month plus a $149 activation fee when you pass, or $95 a month with no activation fee, and publishes a route to a live account. Both use a $2,000 end-of-day trailing drawdown on 50K and pay 90%.
body:
Which to pick

Pick Lucid if you want one payment and a short path to payouts. LucidFlex pays any day after 5 days of $150 or more, up to 50% of profit and $2,000 per request, and moves the account to live after 5 payouts. Pick Topstep if you expect to pass quickly and want the lowest entry price: one month on the Standard path plus activation costs $198.

Rules that trip people up

Topstep's Combine has a best-day limit of 55% of the profit target; going over raises the target instead of failing you. The LucidFlex evaluation uses a 40% rule. Lucid closes open positions at 4:45 PM ET, while Topstep wants you flat by 3:10 PM CT. Lucid allows bots and trade copiers but bans HFT; Topstep allows automated strategies only through its TopstepX API, and not on live accounts.

verdict: Both sell one-time 50K evaluations with a $3,000 target and a $2,000 max loss. Lucid publishes its price ($136 for LucidFlex), uses end-of-day drawdown on every plan and has no consistency rule on LucidFlex once funded. Apex did not show its current 50K evaluation prices when we checked, has no consistency rule in the evaluation, and lets you choose end-of-day or intraday trailing drawdown.
body:
Which to pick

Pick Lucid if you want a known price, end-of-day drawdown and bots allowed. Pick Apex if you want its payout ladder: the 50K end-of-day account pays $1,500 rising to $3,000 per request, but you need a $52,600 balance to request and the account closes after six payouts. LucidFlex caps each request at $2,000 and moves you to live after 5 payouts.

Rules that trip people up

On an Apex funded account no single day may be 50% or more of the profit since your last payout. Apex bans automation entirely; Lucid allows bots and copiers but not HFT or microscalping. Both make you close before the end of the session: Lucid at 4:45 PM ET, Apex before market close.

verdict: FTMO's 2-Step costs €345 for 50K with a static 10% max loss and no consistency rule, and the fee is refunded with your first reward. E8 One costs $288 and by default uses a 6% drawdown that trails the highest closed balance, with the rules configurable at checkout. FTMO has run since 2015 and is rated 4.8 on Trustpilot.
body:
Which to pick

Pick FTMO for a loss limit that never moves, no consistency rule and a long track record. Its 1-Step (€319) trails end-of-day by 10% and has a 50% best-day rule. Pick E8 if you want to set drawdown, split (up to 100%) or payout speed yourself. E8 Pro ($228) has a static 8% max loss and daily payouts, but caps daily profit at $1,000.

Rules that trip people up

E8 One adds a 40% consistency rule in the performance stage. On news, FTMO funded accounts may not execute orders 2 minutes before or after selected high-impact releases, while E8 One performance accounts are blocked from 5 minutes before to 5 minutes after.

verdict: FXIFY's 50K One Phase and Two Phase both cost $379, and its homepage says EAs are allowed, including grid and martingale. FTMO's 2-Step costs €345 with a static 10% max loss, no consistency rule and the fee refunded with the first reward. FXIFY does not accept US residents; FTMO does.
body:
Which to pick

Pick FTMO for its track record (since 2015), its 4.8 Trustpilot score against FXIFY's 4.3, or if you live in the US. Pick FXIFY if you run EAs, or want a one-phase account whose 6% drawdown trails the closed balance and locks at the starting balance. FXIFY's Two Phase has a static 10% max loss, like FTMO's 2-Step.

How much you can hold

FTMO caps you at $400,000 per trader or strategy before scaling. FXIFY lets you hold one active account per account size, up to $400K.

verdict: Blue Guardian's 2 Step Standard costs $232 for 50K against €345 for FTMO's 2-Step. Both use a static max loss: $4,000 (8%) at Blue Guardian and 10% at FTMO. Blue Guardian pays 85% every 14 days and charges 3% on payouts; FTMO pays 80% (90% with scaling) from day 14 and says it charges no withdrawal commission.
body:
Which to pick

Pick Blue Guardian if the entry price matters most. Pick FTMO for the larger loss limit, the fee refunded with your first reward and a 4.8 Trustpilot score.

Rules that trip people up

On funded accounts Blue Guardian blocks opening or closing trades within 5 minutes of high-impact news and FOMC; FTMO's window is 2 minutes around selected releases. Blue Guardian flags trades shorter than 2 minutes as tick scalping and bans HFT and arbitrage bots.

verdict: Blueberry's cheapest 50K, the 1-Step, costs $302.50 with a static 6% max loss; its Prime 2-Step costs $406 with a static 10%. FTMO's 2-Step costs €345 with a static 10% and refunds the fee with the first reward. Blueberry does not accept US residents and had no Trustpilot rating when we checked; FTMO accepts US traders and is rated 4.8.
body:
Which to pick

Pick Blueberry Prime if you want no risk-per-trade limit and no lot restriction, with payouts every 14 days after 3 active days. Its Flex 1-Step gives a 12% static max loss ($6,000) for $490, but bans weekend holding and caps risk at 1% per trade idea. Pick FTMO for the lower price on a 10% static account, the fee refund and the longer track record.

Rules that trip people up

Blueberry bans opening or closing trades from 2 minutes before to 2 minutes after high-impact news on every account; on Prime only new positions are blocked. FTMO applies its 2-minute news rule on funded accounts only.

blurb: Monthly with no activation fee vs one-time
verdict: Alpha Futures' Standard plan costs $129 a month for 50K with no activation fee and an end-of-day drawdown that stops at the starting balance. Apex sells one-time evaluations with a choice of end-of-day or intraday drawdown, but did not show its current 50K prices when we checked. Both ban bots and full automation.
body:
Which to pick

Pick Alpha Futures for no activation fee and up to 4 payouts a month, each after 5 winning days of $200 or more ($500 minimum, $3,000 maximum on 50K Standard). Pick Apex if you want no consistency rule in the evaluation. Its funded account pays $1,500 rising to $3,000 per request, but closes after six payouts.

Rules that trip people up

Alpha Futures' Standard plan has a 50% consistency rule in the evaluation and 40% once qualified. On Standard, Zero and Direct qualified accounts it bans orders from 2 minutes before to 2 minutes after red-folder news. Apex allows news trading as part of a normal strategy. Alpha closes every position by 4:20 PM ET.

blurb: Pick your payout cycle vs fee refunded
verdict: Both sell a 50K two-step with 8% and 5% targets and a static 10% max loss ($5,000). FundingPips' 2 Step Standard costs $349 and lets you trade split for speed: 60% weekly, 80% bi-weekly or 100% on demand. FundedNext's Stellar 2-Step costs $299.99, pays 80% after 21 days and then every 14, and refunds the fee with the first reward.
body:
Which to pick

Pick FundedNext for the lower price, the fee refund and US access; it is rated 4.5 on Trustpilot from more than 80,000 reviews. Pick FundingPips if faster payouts matter more than the split. Its on-demand option pays 100% but adds a 35% consistency rule.

Rules that trip people up

FundingPips funded (Master) accounts close positions every day unless you buy a holding add-on; FundedNext allows overnight and weekend holding. FundedNext does not allow EAs on accounts of $50K and above; FundingPips allows your own automated EA with proof of ownership.

verdict: The5ers' High Stakes costs $249 (New) or $279 (Classic) for 50K, with a static 8% max loss and payouts capped at $3,000 per request. FXIFY's Two Phase costs $379 with a static 10% max loss, and its One Phase trails the closed balance by 6%. The5ers needs written approval for any automated trading; FXIFY's homepage says EAs, including grid and martingale, are allowed.
body:
Which to pick

Pick The5ers for the lower price, a scaling plan that lifts the split to 100%, and a record going back to 2016 with a 4.7 Trustpilot score. Pick FXIFY if you trade with EAs or want the larger 10% static loss limit.

Rules that trip people up

The5ers charges 3.5% on Rise, crypto and bank payouts (Hub Credits are free) and blocks new orders from 2 minutes before to 2 minutes after high-impact news. FXIFY does not accept US residents.

blurb: Cheaper with payout fees vs fee refunded
verdict: Aqua Funded's 2 Step Standard costs $239 for 50K with a static 8% max loss ($4,000) and a 90% split, but takes a 3% processing fee from every payout. FTMO's 2-Step costs €345 with a static 10% max loss, pays 80% (90% with scaling) and refunds the fee with the first reward. Aqua had no Trustpilot rating when we checked; FTMO is rated 4.8.
body:
Which to pick

Pick Aqua Funded for the lower price, the higher split, instant-funding options and bots allowed for your own strategy. Pick FTMO for the larger loss limit, no withdrawal commission and the longer track record.

Rules that trip people up

On Aqua accounts from April 27, 2026, profit from trades within 5 minutes of red-folder news or FOMC is capped at 0.5% of the starting balance per payout cycle. FTMO funded accounts may not execute orders 2 minutes before or after selected high-impact news. Aqua allows weekend holding on every account; FTMO only in the challenge and on Swing accounts.
